events.title: Louis Blériot Crosses the English Channel
events.description: French aviator Louis Blériot flew his Blériot XI monoplane from Calais, France, to Dover, England, in about 36 minutes, becoming the first person to cross the English Channel in a heavier-than-air aircraft and winning a £1,000 prize offered by the Daily Mail.
events.significance: The flight showed the practical potential of aviation, ended Britain's perception of itself as an island safe from attack, and boosted the growth of the aircraft industry.

events.title: Birth of Louise Brown, the First 'Test-Tube Baby'
events.description: Louise Joy Brown was born at Oldham General Hospital in England. She was the first human born after conception by in vitro fertilization (IVF), a procedure developed by Robert Edwards and Patrick Steptoe.
events.significance: Her birth opened the era of assisted reproductive technology, which has helped millions of people conceive. Robert Edwards received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 2010.

events.title: Mussolini Removed from Power in Italy
events.description: After the Allied invasion of Sicily and a vote of no confidence by the Grand Council of Fascism, King Victor Emmanuel III dismissed Benito Mussolini as prime minister and had him arrested. Marshal Pietro Badoglio was appointed to lead the government.
events.significance: The fall of Mussolini ended over two decades of Fascist rule, led to Italy's armistice with the Allies in September 1943, and altered the course of World War II in Europe.

events.title: Battle of Lundy's Lane
events.description: American and British forces fought near Niagara Falls in one of the bloodiest battles of the War of 1812. It was fought into the night and ended in a tactical draw, with heavy casualties on both sides.
events.significance: The battle halted American attempts to invade Upper Canada and strengthened Canadian resolve and identity. It remains among the deadliest engagements fought on Canadian soil.

events.title: Tunisia Abolishes the Monarchy and Becomes a Republic
events.description: Tunisia's Constituent Assembly voted to abolish the monarchy of Muhammad VIII al-Amin, the Bey of Tunis, and proclaimed the country a republic. Habib Bourguiba became its first president.
events.significance: The move completed Tunisia's transition after gaining independence from France in 1956 and set up the republic that Bourguiba led for 30 years.
